ai.literal: If they see a fitting opportunity, for striking, an anvil is the friendship of those who do not inwardly agree but outwardly associate closely.
ai.translation: The friendship of those who do not inwardly agree but outwardly behave smoothly is like an anvil, serving only to hold you still until they find the fitting opportunity to strike.
ai.modern: மனதால் ஒன்றாமல், வெளியில் மட்டும் நெருங்கிப் பழகுபவர்களின் நட்பு, தகுந்த சமயம் கிடைக்கும்போது நம்மை அடித்து வீழ்த்துவதற்குப் பயன்படும் பட்டடை போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against insincere friendship. The poet compares the friendship of insincere people—who pretend to be close but do not truly align in heart—to an anvil. Just as an anvil holds a piece of metal firmly in place only so that the hammer can strike it, these false friends maintain a close relationship only to keep you within reach until they find the perfect opportunity to strike and ruin you. The key words 'நேரா' (not inwardly agreeing) and 'நிரந்தவர்' (outwardly behaving smoothly) highlight the contrast between their inner hostility and outer friendliness.

ai.literal: The friendship of those who resemble kin but are not kin, like the mind of women, will become different.
ai.translation: The friendship of those who pretend to be your kin but are not, will constantly shift and change like the minds of fickle women.
ai.modern: உறவினரைப் போல நடித்து, உண்மையில் உறவினர் அல்லாதவர்களின் நட்பு, பெண்களின் மனத்தைப் போல மாறிக்கொண்டே இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us about the unstable nature of false friends. The poet describes them as people who outwardly act like our own kin ('inam pōṉṟu') but are actually not ('inam allār'). Their friendship ('kēṇmai') is compared to the shifting minds of women ('makaḷir maṉam'), which are depicted here as changing easily. Just as those minds lack constancy, the affection of false friends will eventually alter and turn different ('vēṟupaṭum') when circumstances change.

ai.literal: Even though having learned many good things, becoming good of mind is impossible for enemies.
ai.translation: Even when they have learned many good and noble things, it is impossible for those who harbor hostility to become pure of heart.
ai.modern: பல நல்ல விஷயங்களைக் கற்றறிந்த போதிலும், பகைவர்கள் மனத்தால் நல்லவர்களாக மாறுவது அரிதானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the difficulty of reforming a hostile mind through mere education. The word 'மாணார்' refers to enemies or those who do not align in true friendship. Even if such people have studied many good and noble books ('பலநல்ல கற்றக் கடைத்து'), their inner nature remains unchanged. The poet emphasizes that external learning does not automatically result in a good heart ('மனநல்லர் ஆகுதல்'), making it dangerous to trust them based solely on their education.

ai.literal: With the face sweetly smiling, in the mind bitter, deceitful people, to fear is fit.
ai.translation: One must fear the deceitful who smile sweetly with their face but harbor bitterness in their hearts.
ai.modern: முகத்தால் இனிமையாகச் சிரித்து, மனதில் தீமையை வைத்திருக்கும் வஞ்சகர்களைக் கண்டு அஞ்ச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us about the danger of false friends. The key contrast is between the face (முகம்) and the heart or mind (அகம்). Deceitful people (வஞ்சர்) show a sweet, smiling countenance (இனிய நகாஅ) outwardly, but harbor bitter, hostile intentions (இன்னா) inwardly. The poet emphasizes that we must fear (அஞ்சப் படும்) such hypocrites because their hidden malice is far more dangerous than open enmity.

ai.literal: Those who do not fit in their mind, even in the slightest measure, by their words, to trust is not the right way.
ai.translation: It is never right to trust those whose minds do not agree with you, no matter how much they promise with their words.
ai.modern: மனதால் நம்மோடு பொருந்தாதவர்களை, அவர்கள் கூறும் சொற்களைக் கொண்டு எவ்வகையிலும் நம்புவது தகுதியற்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us against trusting insincere people whose inner minds do not align with their outward behavior. The phrase 'மனத்தின் அமையாதவர்' refers to those whose hearts are not truly united or in harmony with us. Even if they speak sweet, reassuring words, one should not rely on them in the slightest degree. True friendship requires a union of minds, and relying merely on verbal assurances from those who are mentally detached is a path to deception.

ai.literal: Like friends good things even if they speak, enemies' words quickly to be understood will be.
ai.translation: Even if those who are hostile speak beneficial things like friends, the true nature of their words will be quickly understood.
ai.modern: நண்பர்களைப் போல நல்ல காரியங்களைச் சொன்னாலும், நம்முடன் மனதால் ஒன்றாத பகைவர்களின் சொற்களின் உண்மைத் தன்மை விரைவில் உணர்ந்து கொள்ளப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the deceptive words of insincere people who pretend to be friends. Even if they offer advice or speak words that seem highly beneficial on the surface, their underlying hostile intent cannot remain hidden. A discerning mind will quickly perceive the true, harmful nature behind their sweet words. The key words 'oṭṭār' (those who do not unite in heart) and 'ollai' (quickly) emphasize that the false nature of an enemy's speech is rapidly exposed to those who are vigilant.

ai.literal: Word humility from enemies do not accept; bow bending harm because of intending.
ai.translation: Do not accept the humble words of your enemies; the bending of a bow is only for bringing about harm.
ai.modern: பகைவர்களிடம் காணப்படும் பணிவான சொற்களை நம்பி ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளக் கூடாது; ஏனெனில், வில் வளைவது தீமை செய்வதற்காகவே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us not to trust the polite or submissive words of an enemy. The poet uses a brilliant double meaning of the word 'vaṇakkam', which means both 'humility' (in speech) and 'bending' (of an object). Just as the bending of a bow is not a sign of respect but a preparation to shoot a lethal arrow, the humble speech of an adversary is merely a prelude to causing harm. Therefore, one must remain vigilant and not be deceived by superficial sweetness.

ai.literal: Even inside the folded hands (of worship), a weapon will be hidden; the wept tears of enemies are also like that.
ai.translation: A weapon may lie hidden even within the clasped hands of worshipping foes; the tears they weep are of the very same deceptive nature.
ai.modern: பகைவர்கள் வணங்கித் தொழும் கைகளின் உள்ளேயும் கொலைக்கருவி மறைந்திருக்கும்; அவர்கள் அழுது சிந்தும கண்ணீரும் அத்தகையதே (வஞ்சனை உடையதே).
ai.explanation: This couplet warns us to be extremely cautious of the outward displays of submission or grief shown by our adversaries. The poet uses the powerful image of hands folded in worship (தொழுதகை) to show how gestures of respect can literally hide a weapon (படை) meant for our destruction. In the same manner, the tears (கண்ணீர்) shed by an enemy are not signs of genuine remorse or sorrow, but are equally deceptive tools used to disarm our vigilance. We must look past these superficial behaviors to protect ourselves from hidden hostility.

ai.literal: Making excessively (outwardly), those who despise themselves (inwardly), making (them) smile, within friendship, to embrace (them) to death is the proper way.
ai.translation: With those who outwardly display excessive affection but inwardly despise you, it is fitting to make them smile with outward friendliness, yet embrace them to their ruin within that very friendship.
ai.modern: வெளிப்படையாகப் பெரிதும் அன்பு காட்டி, மனத்திற்குள் நம்மை இகழ்பவர்களை, நாமும் முகமலர்ச்சி அடையச் செய்து, அந்த நட்பிற்குள்ளேயே அவர்களை அழிப்பதே தகுதியானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to deal with deceitful, feigned friends. The poet describes enemies who pretend to be highly affectionate ('mika ceytu') but secretly hold contempt ('tam eḷḷuvārai'). The strategy to counter them is to reciprocate their behavior: make them smile outwardly ('naka ceytu') while maintaining the guise of friendship ('naṭpiṉuḷ'), but ultimately deliver a fatal blow or neutralize them ('cā pullal' - embracing to death or ruin). It emphasizes that deceit must be met with strategic, protective deceit to ensure one's own survival.

ai.literal: When the time comes that enmity becomes friendship, befriending with the face, avoiding friendship of the heart, one should abandon them.
ai.translation: When a time comes where enemies pretend to be friends, one should reciprocate friendship only with a smiling face, while completely avoiding any true friendship of the heart.
ai.modern: பகைவர் நண்பராக நடிக்கும் காலம் வரும்போது, முக அளவில் மட்டும் நட்பு காட்டி, மனப்பூர்வமான நட்பைத் தவிர்த்து அவர்களை விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises how to deal with insincere or hostile alliances. When circumstances force an enemy to seek your friendship, you should not reject them openly; instead, show a friendly face (முகநட்டு) to maintain appearances. However, you must strictly avoid establishing any genuine, deep friendship of the heart (அகநட்பு ஒரீஇ) with them. Ultimately, you must keep them at a distance and let them go, as their inner hostility remains unchanged.
